::: {.project-card}
### Wolf pup survival in northeastern Minnesota

Using radio-collared wolf pups from one of the longest-running wolf studies, in the Superior National Forest (1970 to 2017), I estimate how many pups survived their first two years, when and how they died, and how body condition and roads shaped their risk. Data from the U.S. Geological Survey Wolf and Deer Project (Mech 2009, 2022; Barber-Meyer et al. 2021).

[Poster and results](projects/snf-wolf-pups/index.qmd)
:::

::: {.project-card}
### White-tailed deer {#white-tailed-deer}

My graduate research at UBC Okanagan examines the drivers of white-tailed deer range expansion in the Columbia Mountains of British Columbia, including winter severity, resource availability, and predator abundance, using trail-camera data and statistical modelling. I wrote the project's Mitacs Accelerate grant ($75,000, 2024), in partnership with Biodiversity Pathways Ltd.

The camera network spans more than 7,000 km² of the Columbia Mountains and combines cameras run by Parks Canada, Biodiversity Pathways, and Splatsin, whose ten sites have run since 2017. The work takes place on unceded Secwépemc, Sinixt, Syilx, and Ktunaxa territories.

[Project page](projects/wtd-expansion/index.qmd)
:::

As an Applied Ecologist with [SwampDonkey](https://www.swampdonkeysolutions.ca/), I support ecosystem and wildlife research and monitoring in western Canada.
